we have developed a system for the efficient production of minigene containing retroviral vectors.

the insertion of genomic gene elements (minigenenes) into retroviral vector constructs can increase the synthesis of transgenes and that the use of a cytoplasmically replicating alphavirus/retrovector system can facilitate the production of retroviral vectors containing minigenes.
In summary, our research is concerned with
the production of retroviral vectors containing genomic gene elements.
developing a system that will facilitate the synthesis of minigene-promoted retrovirus vectors.
the development of a new gene transfer system for the production of human clotting factor proteins in transduced cells.
In summary, a comprehensive and detailed conclusive statement would be that
the alphavirus/retrovector hybrid system is a useful tool for the production of minigene containing retroviral vectors.
the alphavirus/retrovector system is an efficient means of producing minigene-containing recombinant retrovirus.

the use of minigenes in retroviral vectors is a viable strategy for the expression of human clotting factor genes and that the use of an alphavirus/ retrovirus hybrid vector system can overcome the problems associated with the insertion of a minigene into a retroviral vector.
A comprehensive summary for our work would be that
the use of an alphavirus/ retrovirus hybrid vector system to produce minigene-containing vectors can result in increased levels of factor VIII and factor IX proteins in transduced cells.
we developed a system to generate minigene-containing, alphavirus/retrovector particles.
the use of an alphavirus/ retrovirus hybrid vector system to synthesize minigene-containing vector RNA in the cell cytoplasm results in increased production of factor VIII or factor XI proteins.
The main takeaway from our work is that
the use of a hybrid vector system can be used to increase the efficiency of minigene transfer into retroviral vector systems.
the use of alphavirus/retovirus hybrids for production of retroviral vectors can be used to produce retroviral vectors containing minigene sequences.
the alphavirus/retrotrovirus hybrid vector can be used to produce minigene-containing vectors that can be used to transduce cells with stable expression of the minigenes.
